tagline: Akvan hits Odisha; missiles strike Kyiv bridges; Asia stocks plunge

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan makes landfall at Gopalpur
stories.dek: IMD says Akvan crossed near Gopalpur at 7:30–8:30, gusting 90 km/h, after 300,000 were evacuated.
stories.scene: A grey cyclone eye over a flooded coastal highway, evacuation buses, and palm trees bent flat at Gopalpur.

stories.headline: Russian missiles hit three Kyiv bridges
stories.dek: Mayor Klitschko says missiles hit three Dnipro bridges, killing 3 people and injuring about 15.
stories.scene: Three river bridges over the Dnipro, one span closed, smoke, and emergency crews on the bank.

stories.headline: Asian markets plunge on AI fears
stories.dek: Al Jazeera says the Nikkei fell as much as 4.9% and the Kospi 5.4% on Friday.
stories.scene: A Tokyo trading-floor board glowing red, with chip-stock names and a steep downward chart.

stories.headline: COP31 final day faces a thin draft
stories.dek: A draft released Thursday drops fossil fuels and a $120 billion goal as Friday's close nears.
stories.scene: Delegates under a COP31 banner in Antalya, a draft text with fossil-fuel lines crossed out.

stories.headline: Italy's unions stage a nationwide strike
stories.dek: CGIL's strike covers the working day, with marches planned in about 100 squares, Adnkronos says.
stories.scene: Union banners reading The future is now filling a Rome square, with idle buses behind them.

stories.headline: UK and EU near 100,000 youth cap
stories.dek: The BBC says each side would take up to 100,000 young people a year, with talks down to the wire.
stories.scene: UK and EU flags on a Brussels table beside a draft cap marked 100,000.

stories.headline: Japan core inflation rises to 2.2%
stories.dek: Core CPI, excluding fresh food, rose 2.2% on the year in October, below a 2.3% forecast.
stories.scene: A Tokyo price board for rice and fuel beside a chart ticking up to 2.2 percent.

stories.headline: China holds benchmark loan rates again
stories.dek: The one-year loan prime rate stays at 3.0% and the five-year rate at 3.5%, the PBOC says.
stories.scene: The People's Bank of China facade and a rate card stuck at 3.0 and 3.5 percent.

stories.headline: Phillips scores a Wellington Test century
stories.dek: AP reports Phillips out for 118 in Wellington, a Test hundred after his ODI and T20I tons.
stories.scene: A batsman raising his bat at Basin Reserve, scoreboard showing 118, India fielders around.

stories.headline: US warns AUKUS sub sales would hurt
stories.dek: The CBO says selling Australia 3 to 5 Virginia-class submarines would shrink the US fleet for years.
stories.scene: A Virginia-class submarine beside a US Navy tally with several hulls marked as transferred.

stories.headline: UN Security Council holds a straw poll
stories.dek: Grynspan led 7 of 8 straw polls; Friday's ballot separates the 5 permanent members' votes.
stories.scene: A Security Council horseshoe, secret ballots, and a name card for Rebeca Grynspan.

stories.headline: Pill makes some pancreatic tumours vanish
stories.dek: In a 61-patient trial, cancer became undetectable in one in 12 people given daraxonrasib, the BBC says.
stories.scene: A daily pill bottle, a scan with a tumour fading, and a lab bench at a cancer centre.

stories.headline: Trump delays decision on new Iran strikes
stories.dek: Trump told Reuters he would discuss fresh large Iran strikes after the start of 2027.
stories.scene: A White House podium and a map of Iran with a hold stamp across fresh strike markers.

stories.headline: Malawi drivers queue through the night for fuel
stories.dek: A driver in Blantyre paid about $17.31 for two litres on the black market, Al Jazeera reports.
stories.scene: A night queue of cars at a Blantyre pump and a jerrycan changing hands at the roadside.

stories.headline: Africa presses Europe on climate cash
stories.dek: Day 12 in Antalya: the BBC says Africa wants more climate cash and Europe says use funds already pledged.
stories.scene: African delegates at a COP31 microphone opposite a European Union nameplate.

stories.headline: Gaza rescuers lose most of their trucks
stories.dek: Al Jazeera says more than 85% of Gaza Civil Defence vehicles are out of service.
stories.scene: A row of broken civil-defence trucks in Gaza, one hood open, rescue gear on the ground.

stories.headline: Iraqi students protest classroom gender split
stories.dek: As many as 400 women have protested for two weeks after Al-Qadisiyah University removed male professors, the Guardian says.
stories.scene: Students with placards outside a university gate, classroom doors marked men and women.

stories.headline: China warns citizens off winter Fuji climbs
stories.dek: China's embassy warns against winter Fuji climbs as a family offers a $75,000 reward.
stories.scene: Snowy Mount Fuji, a missing-person poster, and a Chinese embassy warning notice.

stories.headline: Britain quietly secures supermarket fridges
stories.dek: The BBC says the operation covered 10,000s of supermarket fridges at risk from hackers.
stories.scene: Rows of supermarket freezer cabinets and a technician locking a remote temperature controller.

stories.headline: BepiColombo nears orbit after eight years
stories.dek: BepiColombo is about to orbit Mercury after eight years and almost 10 billion kilometres, the BBC says.
stories.scene: A twin-probe spacecraft approaching grey, cratered Mercury, Sun glaring behind it.

stories.headline: Army delays Iowa blast of 5 tons
stories.dek: The US army postponed a noon Friday blast of about 5 tons of lead azide in Middletown, the Guardian says.
stories.scene: Crates marked lead azide in an Iowa field, a noon blast crossed out, houses nearby.

stories.headline: Russell tops wet Las Vegas practice
stories.dek: George Russell topped rain-hit practice 2 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the BBC says.
stories.scene: A silver Mercedes on a wet night street circuit, neon signs reflecting on the asphalt.

stories.headline: Rio Tinto pledges $370m for Panguna
stories.dek: ABC reports Rio Tinto pledged $370 million to address the Panguna mine's legacy in Bougainville.
stories.scene: A scarred open-pit mine in jungle hills and a pledge document marked 370 million dollars.

stories.headline: HMCS Spitfire wreck found after 128 years
stories.dek: ABC says the 19-metre HMCS Spitfire was found off Queensland 128 years after it sank.
stories.scene: A sonar image of a small wooden warship on the seabed off the Queensland coast.

stories.headline: Woman guilty of killing parents with insulin
stories.dek: A South Australian jury convicted Raelene Polymiadis after a four-month trial of killing her 94-year-old parents.
stories.scene: A courtroom dock, insulin vials on an evidence table, and a jury box.

stories.headline: Grant cut puts $600m incinerator in doubt
stories.dek: ABC says a federal grant for a $600 million waste incinerator at Maryvale was quietly terminated.
stories.scene: A mill site in the Latrobe Valley with a cancelled grant stamp over incinerator plans.

stories.headline: Missing hunter found alive near Darwin
stories.dek: Police say a 45-year-old hunter was found alive after almost 24 hours near Marrakai, the ABC reports.
stories.scene: A search helicopter over scrub near a national park and a hunter walking out with rescuers.

stories.headline: Haiti police say raid killed 34 gunmen
stories.dek: Haitian police say at least 34 gang members were killed in a raid in Port-au-Prince, Al Jazeera reports.
stories.scene: Armoured police vehicles on a Port-au-Prince street after a night raid.

stories.headline: Patient file reached over 100,000 NHS staff
stories.dek: The Guardian says the ICO opened an inquiry after one patient's records reached more than 100,000 NHS staff.
stories.scene: A hospital computer screen with a patient file shared across a huge staff directory.

stories.headline: Police kill wanted suspect in Bulandshahr raid
stories.dek: Police say officers killed Naseem Durrani, who had a 50,000-rupee reward and over 25 cases, on Friday.
stories.scene: Police tape across a night street in Bulandshahr and an evidence marker on the road.

stories.headline: Gold slides toward a $3,500 low
stories.dek: FXStreet says gold fell toward $3,500 in Asian trade, its lowest since September 2025.
stories.scene: Gold bars on a desk beside a chart falling toward 3,500 dollars an ounce.

stories.headline: New Hunger Games film opens in cinemas
stories.dek: A Hunger Games prequel set 24 years before the first film is released in cinemas today, the BBC says.
stories.scene: A cinema marquee for a Hunger Games prequel and a queue under neon lights.

stories.headline: Trust pays after Palestine-badge Prevent threat
stories.dek: The Guardian says one trust will pay tens of thousands after threatening 4 pupils over Palestine badges.
stories.scene: Four school badges in Palestinian colours beside a Prevent referral letter marked withdrawn.

stories.headline: BBC hears from seven people inside Taiz
stories.dek: The BBC spoke to 7 people trapped in Houthi-besieged Taiz about life under fire.
stories.scene: A damaged street in a besieged city, a phone interview, and a child covering their ears.

stories.headline: Bitcoin slips under $61,560 on Friday
stories.dek: FXStreet says bitcoin slipped below $61,560 on Friday, its lowest level since early July.
stories.scene: A crypto price screen in red, bitcoin under 61,560, traders watching phones.

stories.headline: Olympic whitewater costs stay secret
stories.dek: A 2032 Olympic whitewater venue in Redlands is an election fight while its costs stay secret, the ABC says.
stories.scene: A whitewater channel model, an Olympic 2032 mark, and a budget page blacked out.

date_check.item: Trump-Xi-Putin meeting and peace declaration in Shenzhen
Anthropic Nasdaq debut: priced at $83, closed up 17% at $97.17, about a $107.3 billion IPO
date_check.note: Thursday 19 November. The first full US session had not opened by about 06:30 UTC Friday, so no Friday trading result is confirmed.

date_check.item: GTA VI midnight launch; BBC later estimated sales above $2.3 billion
date_check.note: Launch was Thursday 19 November. Left out of Friday stories.

date_check.item: ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
date_check.note: Thursday 19 November. Friday pieces are reaction, not the ruling.

date_check.item: US Senate vote blocking an Iran war-powers resolution, 48-51
date_check.note: Thursday 19 November, about 20:00 UTC. Some Friday datelines repeat it.

date_check.item: Daytime Russian drones in Kyiv damaging the Dutch and Austrian embassies and St Volodymyr's Cathedral, one person killed
date_check.note: Thursday 19 November. Friday's separate story is the overnight ballistic attack on three bridges.

date_check.item: Migrant boat capsized off Yenne, Senegal; four bodies later reported
date_check.note: Capsize was overnight Tuesday to Wednesday. Al Jazeera says the toll of four was confirmed to Reuters on Thursday.

date_check.item: Colombia tax protests in Bogota and other cities
date_check.note: Al Jazeera says the marches were on Thursday.

date_check.item: Lula visits Chief Raoni and Brazil recognises Kapot Nhinore
date_check.note: The visit and ceremony were on Thursday.

date_check.item: Bukele expected to register a third-term bid
date_check.note: Al Jazeera says Thursday was the registration deadline. Wikipedia's 19 November page already records the filing.

date_check.item: Democrats say Kirkland & Ellis gave $11.8 million in free work
date_check.note: The lawmakers' statement was released Thursday.

date_check.item: Meta says it is rethinking its 2030 net-zero goal; 2025 emissions 11.8 million tonnes, up 45%
date_check.note: The sustainability report comments were on Thursday.

date_check.item: Berlin coalition summit, Kushner on a Nato-like guarantee, and the Shenzhen peace text
date_check.note: Thursday. A Friday Guardian briefing repeats them beside the new Kyiv bridge attack.

date_check.item: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's Public Investment Fund tower
Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a knitted hat
date_check.note: Guardian story slug is 19 November. A Friday feed repeated it, so it is not used as Friday news.
